_format: Generated by `python3 -m l7r.money export` (gm-assistant features 222, 223); never edit by hand. Per ONE unit of each coin: grams of pure silver; goods dollars (what it bought: the central reading, the geometric mean over the basket's goods at the snapshot, feature 223); goods_dollars_high (the same by the whole basket, the high end of the range); wage dollars (the same share of an unskilled day there, at a US unskilled day's pay); and rokugan_sen (what it bought, in Rokugan's coin: 10 sen a zeni, 10 zeni a bu, 10 bu a koku). Multiply by the amount shown.

beijing-1500.confidence: Rice alone, from the official table of 1497 (an official price). The wage is borrowed: none was found, so it is the Lower Yangzi's of 1573-1620.

tael.note: The Ming treasury tael of the 1500s, 36.9 g

beijing-1615.confidence: Empire-wide rice by reign (a modern silver conversion) with Beijing's official prices of 1615 for salt, sesame oil and firewood, and fish from one secondary report of 1602. The wage is the Lower Yangzi market wage.

tael.note: The Ming treasury tael of the 1500s, 36.9 g

cash.note: About 800 standard cash to the tael in Beijing (the late 1500s' official rate)

beijing-1736.confidence: Allen et al. 2011 (GPIH), a modern reconstruction, at 37 g a tael (rice, millet, oils, fuel). Beans, cloth and flour are left out: priced a kg, a square meter and as flour, not as the basket's liter, length of bolt and grain.

tael.note: Allen et al.'s 37 g (the standard is not named)

cash.note: 800 standard cash to the tael (1737). Beijing's capital cash passed two for one: a sum in capital cash is worth about half

beijing-1820.confidence: Allen et al. 2011 (GPIH), a modern reconstruction, at 37 g a tael (rice, millet, oils, fuel), with the rural Beijing fuel store's cash rate. Salt and fish are Timkovski's Peking market list of 1821, in cash at his own 1,100 a tael; he does not say whether he counts the little string of 500 or the great string of 1,000. His cloth is by the piece of no stated size and is left out; his wood (6 cash a jin) is held, not used, beside Allen's fuel.

cash.note: 1,243 cash to the tael (rural Beijing 1820-1830, 1,159-1,329, at face count: the store's 95-99 cash a day then match Allen's 2.8 g). Beijing's capital cash passed two for one

beijing-1900.confidence: Meng and Gamble's Beijing retail prices in dollars (rice and millet); rent and fuel are left out (a family's, of unknown size).

cash.note: 136-140 coppers of 10 cash to the dollar (1918-1919, the end of the era)

dollar.note: 0.72 tael (the GPIH files' rate, a later Beijing one); Canton's own 1835 figures bracket it at 0.71 and 0.75. Cents are hundredths

canton-1835.confidence: The Chinese Repository's Canton of 1835. Rice is the top of its range. No source gives Canton's cash a tael; its cash is by the dollar, about 1,000 cash (a Canton letter of 1837, and a voyager's round figure for the Guangdong coast in 1832), at 0.72 tael a dollar.

cash.note: About 1,000 cash to the dollar at Canton (Chinese Repository, 1837), so about 1,390 cash to the tael at 0.72 tael a dollar; empire-wide, 1,200-1,500 in 1836-1837

dollar.note: 0.72 tael (the GPIH files' rate, a later Beijing one); Canton's own 1835 figures bracket it at 0.71 and 0.75. Cents are hundredths

osaka-1700.confidence: Priced at the Kyoho coinage of 1722-1735, the era's longest single coinage: Kumon's rice and barley for those years. It is for the years of good silver, 1690-1694 and 1719-1735, whose rice stood within a fifth of Kyoho's (Iwahashi); 1695-1718 and 1736-1739 have eras of their own, at the baser coinages of those years. The wage is borrowed: none was found for these years, so it is the reference day chained back by Kumon's farm-servant wage.

monme.note: Kyoho silver (1722-1735), 3.00 g pure; market rates of 1722-1735

songjiang-1680.confidence: Ye Mengzhu's Songjiang: rice and soybeans by the shi, salt by the jin, at the Qing treasury tael. The wage is borrowed: SILENT for Songjiang, so the Lower Yangzi's.

tael.note: The Qing treasury tael, 37.3 g (the tael these prices were counted in is not stated)

suzhou-1750.confidence: Rice alone, from Qian Yong's Lower Yangzi in normal years of the mid-Qianlong. After 1785 rice and the cash rate both rose (rice 1.9-2.7 taels a shi at 1,300-1,400 cash a tael), so a later amount reads high.

cash.note: About 800 cash to the tael (Jiangnan, 760-840 in the mid-Qianlong; 1,300-1,400 by 1796)

tokyo-1882.confidence: Bassino & Ma's Table 3 retail prices (LTES) for basket A; no price for salt, fuel or housing, so the conversion uses basket A's goods only. Its lamp oil is kerosene and its cloth linen (diagram 0301); its grains are farm-gate ratios to paddy and its fish a wholesale ratio, each times retail rice.
